evidence.observation: The single top-level suite collects nine focused contract cases for the pure tool-execution pipeline (prepare -> before-tool decision -> execute -> finalize -> createToolResultMessage). Each case has an isolated setup (factory call), a single action on the exported primitive, and explicit assertions, which is the exact setup/action/assertion skeleton this checklist is derived from.

Factory returns an AgentHarnessTool named "echo" backed by a TypeBox parameters schema and an async execute that echoes args.value into both text content and details; callers pass Partial overrides to inject prepareArguments, execute spies, or throwing executors. This is the canonical setup fixture that makes each case deterministic and side-effect free.

Builds the provider AgentToolCall (type "toolCall", id "call-1", name "echo", default arguments {value:"input"}) so assertions can pin identity (toHaveBeenCalledOnce, toBe(providerCall)) and tool-result message fields (toolCallId/toolName) to fixed literals.

Helper composing prepareToolCall then applyBeforeToolDecision(undefined) to produce a ClearedToolCall, asserting via isImmediate guards that both stages returned the non-immediate branch. It documents the precondition (clearance) required before executeToolCall/finalizeToolCall actions.

Type guard narrowing the union return of prepareToolCall/applyBeforeToolDecision to the ImmediateToolOutcome branch ("kind" in result). Every call assertion uses it to separate the short-circuit error path from the prepared/cleared path, making the discriminated-union contract explicit.
Normalizes an AgentToolResult into its concatenated text parts, letting assertions compare human-readable output ("done", "partial", "tool failed", "denied") instead of raw content arrays.

Returns createGate().gate, the open admission gate injected into executeToolCall. Cases reuse it to assert the abort signal is forwarded (context.abortSignal === gate.signal) and to drive the abort-first refusal case.

evidence.symbol: it("executes with updates, passes the signal, and ignores late updates")
evidence.observation: Action phase calls executeToolCall(cleared, gate, onUpdate, undefined, invocation, BACKGROUND_CONTEXT) with a vi.fn executor that emits one partial update and captures the callback; lateUpdate is invoked after await to prove the finally-guarded acceptingUpdates flag drops post-execution updates. Asserts call count once, isError false, final text "done", updates length 1 and text "partial".

evidence.symbol: it.each(...)("converts %s tool throws to error output")
evidence.observation: Parameterized case runs both a synchronous thrower and an async thrower through executeToolCall and asserts the shared contract result.isError === true with text(result.result) === "tool failed", showing error normalization is identical across sync/async rejection paths.

evidence.symbol: it("applies patches field by field and constructs the tool-result message")
evidence.observation: Action phase feeds finalizeToolCall an executed result (content "original", isError true) plus an AfterToolPatch overriding content, details, usage, isError, terminate; assertions verify field-by-field replacement on FinalizedToolCall and that createToolResultMessage emits role toolResult, toolCallId "call-1", toolName "echo", patched content/details/usage, isError false, and a timestamp >= before.

evidence.symbol: it("preserves unusual JSON object keys in tool-result details")
evidence.observation: Regression case passes details parsed from '{"__proto__":{"preserved":true}}' through finalizeToolCall and asserts Object.hasOwn(message.details, "__proto__") plus deep equality, pinning prototype-safe key handling in createToolResultMessage.

evidence.symbol: it("normalizes missing content from untyped tools")
evidence.observation: Boundary case casts an executed result with content undefined (as never) through finalizeToolCall and asserts createToolResultMessage(finalized).content equals [], documenting the defensive default in the message constructor.

claims.claim: The focused suite packages/agent/test/harness/execution-tools.test.ts follows a uniform setup/action/assertion structure: deterministic factories (call, tool, effectGate) supply setup, exactly one exported pipeline primitive is invoked per case as the action, and assertions pin concrete values/branches.

Setup fixtures are local factories with override injection: tool() (lines 22-38) wraps an "echo" AgentHarnessTool with TypeBox parameters and accepts Partial overrides, call() (lines 18-20) builds the provider call, and effectGate() (lines 57-59) supplies an open Gate; clearPrepared (lines 50-55) composes prepareToolCall + applyBeforeToolDecision(undefined) to reach the cleared precondition.

Assertions are branch-explicit and value-specific: isImmediate (lines 44-48) narrows the union discriminants and text (lines 40-42) normalizes results, so cases assert exact strings such as "tool failed" (it.each, lines 151-171) and "partial"/"done" (lines 120-149) rather than loose truthiness.

Each pipeline stage has a focused contract case: prepare (line 70), immediate errors (line 87), before-tool block/revalidation (line 104), execution with updates and abort-signal forwarding (line 120), sync/async throw conversion (line 151), abort-first gate refusal (line 173), and field-by-field finalize plus message construction (line 185), including prototype-key preservation (line 235) and missing-content normalization (line 245).

A minimal contract checklist mirroring this file requires: isolated deterministic fixtures per case, one action per exported primitive, explicit discriminated-union branch assertions, exact normalized output strings, and coverage of the error, abort, and boundary branches (unknown tool, invalid args, sync/async throw, abort-first, undefined content, __proto__ keys).

conclusion: packages/agent/test/harness/execution-tools.test.ts is the public acceptance contract for packages/agent/src/harness/execution/tools.ts and effect-gate.ts. It demonstrates a repeatable setup/action/assertion skeleton: (1) setup via local factories call/tool/effectGate and the clearPrepared precondition helper; (2) a single action invoking one exported primitive (prepareToolCall, applyBeforeToolDecision, executeToolCall, finalizeToolCall, createToolResultMessage); (3) assertions that are branch-explicit through the isImmediate type guard and value-specific through the text normalizer, with dedicated cases for immediate errors, before-tool block/revalidation, update callbacks and abort-signal forwarding, sync/async throw conversion, abort-first gate refusal, field-by-field after-tool patching, prototype-safe details keys, and missing-content normalization. The minimal contract-test checklist in .prale-eval/contract-deliverable.md is derived directly from these observations, and every cited range was programmatically re-verified to contain the named symbol.
